---
title: "Macro Monitor: what moved unusually"
subtitle: "The United States and six Southeast Asian economies, each series against its own ten-year history and against its neighbours"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from IPython.display import Markdown
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site

init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

flags, meta = site.load("macro", "flags_latest")
series, series_meta = site.load("macro", "series")
neigh, neigh_meta = site.load("macro", "neighbours")
finding = meta.get("finding")
```

This page does not show what happened in every series. It lists the readings that do not fit:
a monthly move far outside what that series usually does, or one economy moving while its
neighbours did not. Each flag is a question to look into, not an answer.

## Flags on the latest readings

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not meta.get("columns"):
    print(site.empty_state(meta, "Flags"))
elif flags.empty:
    print(f'::: {{.verdict}}\n**Nothing unusual.** None of the {meta["n_series"]} series moved '
          f'by {meta["flag_z"]} spreads or more on its latest reading.\n:::')
else:
    print(f'**{len(flags)} of {meta["n_series"]} series are flagged on their latest reading.**\n')
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
    for kind, title in (("own history", "Against its own history"),
                        ("neighbours", "Against its neighbours")):
        part = flags[flags["kind"] == kind]
        if part.empty:
            continue
        print(f"\n### {title}\n")
        for _, r in part.iterrows():
            print(f'- {site.finding_badge(finding)} {r["sentence"]}')
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if meta.get("columns"):
    print(f'\nA reading is flagged when its surprise is at least {meta["flag_z"]} times the '
          f'series\' usual spread. The rule was fixed before any flag was computed; see '
          f'[how flags are made](../methodology.qmd#macro-monitor) and the '
          f'[24-month backtest](backtest.qmd) for how often flags turn out to be noise.')
```

## Every series, most unusual first

"Spreads" is the latest monthly move minus the usual move, divided by the series' usual
spread. Zero is an ordinary month.

```{python}
if series.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(series_meta, "Series")))
else:
    t = series.assign(
        Flag=series["flagged"].map({True: "Flagged", False: ""}),
        latest_month=pd.to_datetime(series["latest_month"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m"),
    )[["country", "name", "latest_month", "value", "units", "move", "move_unit",
       "expected_move", "z", "Flag"]].rename(columns={
        "country": "Economy", "name": "Series", "latest_month": "Latest month",
        "value": "Value", "units": "Units", "move": "Monthly move", "move_unit": "Move in",
        "expected_move": "Usual move", "z": "Spreads"}).round(
        {"Value": 2, "Monthly move": 2, "Usual move": 2, "Spreads": 1})
    show(t, paging=True, pageLength=25, showIndex=False, classes="display compact")
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not series.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
```

## One economy against the region

For the measures the BIS defines the same way in every country, the chart shows each
economy's surprise in its latest month. A cell far from its row's other cells is an economy
moving against the region.

```{python}
if neigh.empty:
    display(Markdown(site.empty_state(neigh_meta, "Neighbour comparison")))
else:
    last = neigh.sort_values("period").groupby(["country", "indicator"]).tail(1)
    wide = last.pivot(index="name", columns="country", values="own_z").round(1)
    fig = px.imshow(wide, color_continuous_scale="RdBu_r", zmin=-4, zmax=4, text_auto=True,
                    aspect="auto", labels={"color": "Spreads", "x": "", "y": ""})
    fig.update_layout(height=320, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10))
    fig.show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if not neigh.empty:
    print(site.finding_line(finding))
print("\n## Sources and limits\n")
print(site.source_note(meta))
```
